blocks.note: Two per-file-ignore keys collapse onto one path once .agents/ becomes .claude/.

Layer A reaches this repo two ways, and never both at once. On v2 it is the vendored tree under .agents/vendor/harness, which the .agents drop removes here; on main it is the plugin, which nothing else in the tree would enable.

The hooks reach this repo two ways, and never both at once. On v2 they are the vendored .mjs files, wired here by repo-relative path; on main the plugin's own hooks.json supplies them from ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, and the .agents drop has already removed everything this stanza points at. Leaving it would wire four hooks to files that do not exist -- which does not error loudly, it just stops enforcing. Removed as a block rather than by a JSON-aware rule because the generator is one file in three repositories and a new operator would have to be written into all three; a block that goes stale fails the build, which is the same guarantee for none of that cost.

The Codex adapter is dropped on main, so the two files that configure it are not there to gate. Harmless to git -- a pathspec matching nothing is not an error -- but a config naming a path the branch does not have is exactly what test_nothing_points_at_a_directory_that_no_longer_exists exists to refuse, and the next reader would have no way to tell this dangling reference from a real one. JSON carries no comments, so the region markers the .py and .md files use are not available here.

substitutions.note: Every reference to the canonical directory, as a path fragment.
And as a path *segment* — `Path(...) / ".agents" / "hooks"` never contains a slash.
The instruction file itself, in prose and in glob patterns.
